actions.diff:
--- a/base58/__init__.py
+++ b/base58/__init__.py
@@ -97,5 +97,23 @@
-        tables = _encode_tables[alphabet] = (
-            pairs, sq, big, big ** 3, big ** 7, alphabet[0:1])
-    pairs, sq, big, big3, big7, zero = tables
-    parts = []
-    while i >= big7:
+        # base**5 still fits in one internal int digit; long values are
+        # divided by it so each linear-time divmod removes five digits
+        big5 = big * base
+        singles = [alphabet[d:d + 1] for d in range(base)]
+        tables = _encode_tables[alphabet] = (
+            pairs, sq, big, big ** 3, big ** 7, alphabet[0:1],
+            singles, big5, big5 ** 24)
+    pairs, sq, big, big3, big7, zero, singles, big5, wide = tables
+    parts = []
+    while i >= wide:
+        # Long values: eight groups of five digits per pass while at least
+        # 120 digits remain. Each group is two digit pairs and one digit.
+        i, rem = divmod(i, big5)
+        i, rem2 = divmod(i, big5)
+        i, rem3 = divmod(i, big5)
+        i, rem4 = divmod(i, big5)
+        i, rem5 = divmod(i, big5)
+        i, rem6 = divmod(i, big5)
+        i, rem7 = divmod(i, big5)
+        i, rem8 = divmod(i, big5)
+        for r in (rem, rem2, rem3, rem4, rem5, rem6, rem7, rem8):
+            parts += pairs[r % sq], pairs[r // sq % sq], singles[r // big]
+    while i >= big7:

actions.reason: Tried a base**5 divisor (still one internal int digit) for long values in b58encode, so each linear-time divmod removes five digits instead of four, applied only while at least 120 digits remain. Outputs were identical, but it measured worse on every metric: encode_ir 1.0207, decode_ir 1.0119, check_ir 1.0108. The extra digit splitting and table unpacking cost more than the fewer divmods saved on the few long blobs. Reverted. The short-input encode path already does about one divmod per four digits with pair lookups, and earlier setup-level trims measured under 0.3%. I found no change likely to clear 1% on this tip.

journal.text:
Test agent here. I read base58/__init__.py and lineage_bench.py. In b58encode I tried a base**5 divisor for long values. It still fits in one internal int digit. Each linear-time divmod then removes five digits instead of four. I applied it only while at least 120 digits remain. Same bytes out was the bar.

The bar held. Outputs were identical. Speed did not follow. encode_ir went from 208975350 to 213307338, ratio 1.0207. decode_ir came in at 1.0119 and check_ir at 1.0108. The run was rejected for no improvement against a required 0.9900. I reverted the edit and submitted nothing.

What I believe now: fewer divmods do not pay here. Splitting each chunk into digits and unpacking the table cost more than the saved divisions. The loop body matters more than the step count.

Next I will profile the existing four-digit loop. I want to know where its time goes before touching the divisor again.
